title: Product-preserving functors on ringed sites preserve derived inverse limits
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on it. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be an additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] preserving countable products: for every $(M_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$, the canonical map $F(\prod_nM_n)\to\prod_nF(M_n)$ is an isomorphism. Let $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ be its unbounded right derived functor, computed by termwise $F$ on K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor, def-pur-kinjective-complex], in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every inverse sequence $K_n$ with transitions $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ and every derived-limit triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]
$$L\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}L[1],\qquad P=\prod_nK_n,\quad \operatorname{pr}_n s=f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1},$$
the maps $RF(\operatorname{pr}_n)$ identify $RF(P)$ with $\prod_nRF(K_n)$. Under this identification, applying $RF$ to the displayed triangle, with its shift comparison on the last map, gives a derived-limit triangle for $(RF(K_n),RF(f_n))$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. In particular $RF(L)$ is a derived limit of the image tower with projections $RF(\operatorname{pr}_n\circ p)$.

source.place: Tag 08U1, label lemma-RF-commutes-with-Rlim, specialized to module sheaves on a small ringed site and target Ab; the source category is Grothendieck by prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist.

proof.text: Write $Q_{\mathcal A}$ and $Q_{\rm Ab}$ for localization. Products of module sheaves exist sectionwise: $(\prod_n M_n)(U)=\prod_n M_n(U)$ with componentwise action and restrictions. A matching family glues uniquely in each $M_n$, hence in their product; maps into it are precisely families of module-sheaf maps. This verifies the product universal property directly from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the smallness of $\mathcal C$ ensures that every complex in $\mathcal A$ has a K-injective resolution. Choose K-injective complexes $I_n$ and isomorphisms $a_n:Q_{\mathcal A}I_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$. The product complex $I=\prod_n I_n$ exists degreewise by the sectionwise construction above.

source.place: Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck; Tag 08U1, first sentence; ringed-site specialization in sites-cohomology.tex, Section 07A5

proof.text: By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], applied to the abelian category $\mathcal A$ and the set $\mathbf N$, $I$ is K-injective and $Q_{\mathcal A}I$, with the localized coordinate projections $Q_{\mathcal A}(r_n)$, is a product of $Q_{\mathcal A}I_n$. Thus there is a unique product isomorphism $a:Q_{\mathcal A}I\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ with $\operatorname{pr}_n a=a_n Q_{\mathcal A}(r_n)$. Its inverse is obtained from the inverse factor isomorphisms and the product universal property; the two composites are identities because all their projections are identities.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, lemma-product-K-injective, both assertions; also Injectives Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products, product clause

proof.text: Let $\eta_J:Q_{\rm Ab}(FJ)\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}J)$ be the natural derived-functor unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. It is invertible for $J=I,I_n$. The canonical maps $F(I^j)\to\prod_nF(I_n^j)$ are isomorphisms by the hypothesis on $F$. Their coordinates are $F(r_n^j)$, so they commute with differentials: the two composites have coordinate $F(d_{I_n}r_n)=F(r_n d_I)$. They therefore give an isomorphism of complexes $F(I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nF(I_n)$. Abelian groups have exact countable products by [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products]; consequently [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] makes $Q_{\rm Ab}(\prod_nF(I_n))$ a product of the $Q_{\rm Ab}(F(I_n))$, with its localized projections. Transport this product cone along the displayed complex isomorphism, the units $\eta_I,\eta_{I_n}$, and $a,a_n$. Naturality gives $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}r_n)\eta_I=\eta_{I_n}Q_{\rm Ab}(F(r_n))$; combined with the equation for $a$, this says the transported legs are exactly $RF(\operatorname{pr}_n)$. Thus the canonical comparison $e:RF(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P'=\prod_n RF(K_n)$ satisfies $\pi_n e=RF(\operatorname{pr}_n)$.

source.place: Tag 08U1, lemma-RF-commutes-with-Rlim, final paragraph; Derived Categories Tags 070Y and 07KC

proof.text: The source has K-injective resolutions by step 1. The target $\operatorname{Ab}$ has them too: take the site with one object, its identity morphism and only the maximal covering sieve, with ring $\mathbf Z$, and apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. A module sheaf on this site is exactly an abelian group with its unique $\mathbf Z$-action, and maps, differentials, homotopies and quasi-isomorphisms are the usual ones, so the resolution supplied there is a resolution in $\operatorname{Ab}$. Thus both resolution hypotheses in [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] hold. It gives a triangulated $RF$ and its shift isomorphism $\sigma_L:RF(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(L)[1]$. Applying it to the specified triangle gives a distinguished triangle with arrows $RF(p),RF(1-s),\sigma_L RF(\delta)$.

source.place: Tag 08U1, sentence asserting exactness of RF; Tag 079P for the singleton ringed-site specialization

proof.text:
Use the isomorphisms $(1,e,e)$ on the three vertices of this image triangle. The resulting distinguished triangle has arrows $eRF(p)$, $b=eRF(1-s)e^{-1}$ and $\sigma_L RF(\delta)e^{-1}$; it is distinguished by invariance under triangle isomorphisms [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every $n$, additivity and functoriality of $RF$ give
$$\pi_n b=RF(\operatorname{pr}_n(1-s))e^{-1}=RF(\operatorname{pr}_n-f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})e^{-1}=\pi_n-RF(f_n)\pi_{n+1}.$$
The product universal property therefore identifies $b$ with $1-s'$ for the image tower. By [def-weil-derived-limit] the resulting triangle is a derived-limit triangle. Finally $\pi_n eRF(p)=RF(\operatorname{pr}_n)RF(p)=RF(\operatorname{pr}_n\circ p)$, giving precisely the required projections. The formula for the last arrow explicitly includes the shift comparison.

Step 1: sectionwise products in Mod(O) follow directly from the module-sheaf definition (elementary), and prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist gives unbounded K-injective resolutions on a small ringed site. Step 2: lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective (generic 0BK6) gives that the product of the I_n is K-injective and is the product in D(A). Its bridge notion of K-injective agrees with def-pur-kinjective-complex because acyclic complexes are closed under shift. Step 3: the natural unit of def-sfb-right-derived-functor is invertible on K-injectives. F(I) is isomorphic to the product of the F(I_n) as complexes, with the differential check written out. lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core (07KC), with Ab's exact products from lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products, makes the termwise product cone limiting without assuming F(I_n) is K-injective. I recomputed the legs: pi_n e = RF(pr_n). Step 4: lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated needs K-injective resolutions in the target too. The step gets them in Ab from prop-pur applied to the one-object site with the trivial topology and ring Z; the route is roundabout but valid, and the hypothesis is discharged rather than ignored. Step 5 (elementary): the triangle isomorphism (1,e,e) gives last arrow sigma_L RF(delta) e^-1. I recomputed pi_n b = pi_n - RF(f_n) pi_{n+1}, so b = 1-s' with no sign slip, and the projections are RF(pr_n p). Edge cases checked: zero functor, zero tower, zero transitions (derived limit is 0), and non-left-exact F.
